description: ZENITHFORGE is an innovation-driven team participating in NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. Our project, “Flame in Freefall,” explores microgravity combustion data to develop AI-powered insights for improving fire safety in space. We are passionate about space science, artificial intelligence, data analysis, and technology. We welcome enthusiastic teammates skilled in AI/ML, coding, data visualization, web development, space science, and research who want to build impactful solutions together.
summary: A full-stack AI platform that predicts microgravity fire behavior using a 3D WebGL simulator and a strict RAG Hallucination Guard, integrating real experimental data from NASA, ISRO, and JAXA to ensure astronaut safety on future space stations.
details:
The Challenge: The Threat of "Two Flames in Free Fall"

In microgravity, fire behaves counterintuitively. Without buoyancy, flames become spherical, slow-burning, and can enter a "cool flame" state that is invisible to standard smoke detectors. Predicting this behavior is critical to preventing catastrophic events like Apollo 1 on future missions to the Moon and Mars.

Our Solution: TWO-FLAMES-AGENT

TWO-FLAMES-AGENT is a multi-agent AI platform designed to simulate and predict microgravity combustion. It bridges the gap between raw experimental physics and actionable engineering insights.

Key Features:

Interactive 3D Simulator: A real-time WebGL environment where users can adjust Oxygen concentration, Airflow, and Gravity. The system instantly visualizes the flame morphing from a buoyant Earth teardrop (1G) to a spherical orbital diffusion shell (0G).

Multi-Agency Data Engine: We didn't just use NASA data. Our Python Data Engine calculates Limiting Oxygen Concentration (LOC) by integrating:

NASA: Saffire I-IV, Apollo 1, and FLEX droplet experiments.

ISRO: IMEx-2026 Gaganyaan and Bharatiya Antariksh Station (BAS) profiles.

JAXA: FLARE solid material (NOMEX) 3D flame data.

Super Intelligence Layer (RAG Guard): Powered by a local Ollama LLM (Qwen 2.5). The AI is strictly bound by a Retrieval-Augmented Generation guard. It force-calls our data engine for quantitative math, then searches the NASA/ISRO corpus for citations. If it cannot find a valid source, it refuses to answer (guard_passed: false), completely eliminating AI hallucinations.

How it Works:

The system uses a FastAPI backend to orchestrate a tool-calling loop. When a user asks a question, the AI acts as a reasoning agent: it first queries the physics engine for risk calculations, then retrieves exact text citations from our local corpus, and finally generates a verified, cited verdict for the user.

Impact:

TWO-FLAMES-AGENT provides a scalable, international platform for fire safety. It gives engineers at NASA and ISRO an actionable tool to plan safe habitats for the Lunar Gateway and the Bharatiya Antariksh Station.
